conviction_note: The fundamental read is close to a push (-1.0) but the reaction read is materially worse, and I let it veto: on the four 8-K item-2.02 dates that are actually earnings releases (2025-09-23, 2025-12-16, 2026-03-24, 2026-06-23) this stock fell -11.57, -2.54, -4.57 and -6.11 — 0 of 4 up, mean -6.2% — and it goes into this one +8.74% in five sessions on a 15 Sep 8-K whose own words are that the change is 'to the segment names only and do not affect the composition of the segments or the historical financial results'. I emit -4.5 rather than the -6.2 base rate because my sign agrees with a +3.93-point put skew (so part of it is already paid for) and because the bar has been cut 5.1% in 90 days, which lowers the odds of a miss-driven leg down; I emit more than the -3.4 finding sum because this name's own reaction distribution is worse than my evidence and understatement is the documented systematic error here.
bar: $0.75 adjusted EPS on $331.3m revenue, 5 analysts, range $0.72-$0.80 and $317.5-343.0m — two agreeing sources: https://news.alphastreet.com/worthington-enterprises-wor-q1-2027-preview-eps-est-0-75-reports-september-23/ and https://www.benzinga.com/trading-ideas/previews/26/09/61836543/worthington-missed-last-quarters-eps-estimate-by-8-5-can-it-bounce-back-sept-22 (both 2026-09). Company issues no formal EPS guidance, so there is no company guide to sit inside; the year-ago comp is $0.74 adjusted on $303.7m. Consensus has been cut 1.3% in 30 days and 5.1% in 90 days from $0.79.
positioning_check: 3.50% of float short, 5.18 days to cover, 1.06m shares (up from 938,948 prior period) — https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/wor/statistics/ via the sweep row, read 2026-09-22. Light; there is no squeeze mechanism to shrink a negative for. The baseline's skew_25d_vol_points is +3.93, i.e. the option market is paying up for downside, so my negative sign AGREES with the market's one directional statement and is discounted for that. Total front-expiry open interest is only 974 contracts with a put/call OI ratio of 0.16 and an 18.6%-of-mid ATM spread, so the skew is a thin quote, not a crowded hedge. event_implied_move_pct computes to 0.0: the 9.43% straddle is fully explained by 47.3% trailing realised vol, which is itself elevated by the 16 Sep 10% pop — so the chain is carrying no incremental event premium at all.

findings.finding: The +8.74% five-session run-up rests on a 15 Sep 8-K that renames Building Products to 'Building Performance Solutions' and Consumer Products to 'Trade & Specialty Solutions' and states in terms that the change is name-only — 'The changes are to the segment names only and do not affect the composition of the segments or the historical financial results' — yet the stock re-rated ~10% in a day on the data-centre reading of the new name, when the underlying data-centre business was already disclosed on the 24 June call at ~$13m for all of FY2026 and 'at least that much' in Q1 FY2027, i.e. roughly 4% of a $331m quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the four 8-K item-2.02 dates in the baseline that are genuinely earnings releases the stock fell every time: 2025-09-23 -11.57%, 2025-12-16 -2.54%, 2026-03-24 -4.57%, 2026-06-23 -6.11%. The 2025-09-23 print is the same fiscal quarter a year ago and adjusted EPS on it rose from $0.50 to $0.74; the stock still lost 11.57%. Tonight's release is the first set of numbers printed under the new segment names, and there is no data-centre line item in the segment tables for the narrative to land on.
findings.why_not_priced: The price moved, but on a narrative rather than on arithmetic. If the market had priced the arithmetic, a filing that explicitly disclaims any effect on segment composition or historical results would not have added ~10% of market capitalisation in one session, and the stock would not now sit 5.4% off its 52-week high having risen 8.74% in five days into a print it has sold four times running. The number the pop is about ($13m a quarter, guided in June) has been public for three months and is small enough that tonight's segment tables cannot corroborate a re-rating of that size — they can only fail to.
findings.independence: Separately sourced and dated: https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/09/16/why-worthington-enterprises-stock-jumped-10-today/ (2026-09-16) attributes the 10.1% move specifically to the rename and the 10 November Investor Day, and the $13m FY2026 / ~$13m Q1 FY2027 ASME data-centre tank figure comes from a different document, the 24 June Q4 call (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-worthington-enterprises-misses-q4-2026-estimates-shares-fall-93CH-4758299) and the 14 August Canaccord deck 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000108516/000119312526350842/wor-ex99_1.htm). NOTE: this finding absorbs what would otherwise have been a separate positive on the data-centre ramp; they rest on the same disclosure and cannot both be filed.
findings.hedge: The 8:30am 23 Sep call is inside the exit window and management is in pre-Investor-Day promotion mode, so an updated or raised data-centre order number on that call is the live path by which this finding pays nothing or goes positive. That is why the high end of the band is above zero.

findings.finding: Midwest hot-rolled coil hit a four-year high of $1,202.40/short ton on 20 August 2026, roughly $1,200 through late August against about $800 a year earlier (+50% YoY) — squarely across Worthington's June–August fiscal Q1, on a company that converts purchased steel and whose last print was an EPS miss ($0.97 vs $1.06) on a 17% sales gain, i.e. a pure margin failure at lower steel prices than these.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the line the name trades on and it has been punished: 2026-06-23, revenue +17% and adjusted EPS $0.97 against $1.06, stock -6.11%; Building Products adjusted EBIT actually FELL that quarter ($68.5m vs $71.3m) on segment sales up 28%, so the margin compression is already demonstrated and is not a forecast.
findings.why_not_priced: It is partly priced and I have sized it accordingly rather than claiming otherwise — HRC is a public series and the five-estimate consensus has been cut 5.1% in 90 days, which is what analysts marking it down looks like. What is not in the cut is the second-order transmission through the unconsolidated JVs, where Worthington books equity income it does not control: ClarkDietrich's contribution already collapsed to $21.9m in FY2026 from $40.8m in FY2025 and to $6.1m from $12.9m in Q4 alone, and management's answer on the June call was that it is 'pretty confident that's a trough' — a hope, not a number. If this were fully priced the $0.75 consensus would not still imply flat adjusted EPS against a year-ago $0.74 on revenue up 9%.
findings.independence: A direct counterparty has attested the transmission, which is what turns this from a macro hypothesis into a finding: Armstrong World Industries, the 50% partner in WAVE, told the market on 2026-07-28 that August price actions were 'intended to offset rising steel costs' (https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/armstrong-world-q2-2026-slides-record-results-drive-raised-guidance-93CH-4817547). Worthington's own June call independently named 'steel, aluminum, brass, and freight and diesel' inflation. Net of the rest of the company: Consumer Products/Trade & Specialty is ~38% of sales, grew 4% with 10% EBITDA growth in FY2026 and is consumable rather than big-ticket, and Home Depot (+1.7% comps) and Lowe's (+0.2%) printed positive comps for the overlapping period, so the offsetting 38% is stable-to-slightly-up and the finding is sized net of that, not gross.
findings.hedge: Management's own framing on the June call was that a tight steel market 'creates a competitive advantage for us', and rising input prices can produce inventory holding gains; the -1.5 is what survives that counter-argument, not the gross headwind.

findings.finding: WAVE, the 50/50 Armstrong JV that supplied $118.1m of Worthington's equity income in FY2026 against $295.8m of total adjusted EBITDA — about 40% of company earnings — is disclosed by the OTHER partner as improving: Armstrong reported WAVE equity earnings of $2m in calendar Q2 2026 against $1m a year earlier and guided to a step-up in the second half.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: WAVE contribution has been the stated driver of the two prints that did least damage: the 2025-09-23 release credited 'increased contributions from WAVE' and the stock still fell, and Q4 FY2026 WAVE equity income was flat YoY at $32.3m while the stock fell 6.11%. This line has never on the baseline's record been worth a positive reaction on its own, which is the main reason it is sized under a point.
findings.why_not_priced: Five analysts cover Worthington and Armstrong is a different sector with a different analyst set, so the read-through is made by almost nobody; a third party disclosed the direction of ~40% of Worthington's earnings eight weeks before Worthington did. If it were priced, the 90-day estimate trend would not be down 5.1% into a quarter whose largest single earnings contributor a counterparty has said is rising.
findings.independence: Armstrong's own press release carries the same figures: https://s202.q4cdn.com/826259286/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Q2-2026-Press-Release_vF.pdf (2026-07-28). Shares no document with any other finding here except that the AWI steel-cost sentence is also cited in finding 2 — there it is used as counterparty attestation of the cost, here as the level of JV earnings, and the two readings are of different sentences.
findings.hedge: Sized at 0.8 and not higher for a specific reason that is part of the finding rather than an argument against it: Armstrong's 'step-up' is explicitly tied to price actions taken IN August, which land at the very end of Worthington's June–August quarter, so the benefit is mostly a Q2 FY2027 event. What this supports for tonight is that WAVE is not deteriorating, which is worth a small positive and no more.

findings.finding: Worthington signed a Fifth Amended and Restated $500m unsecured revolver on 2026-08-31 with a $300m accordion, pushing maturity from 2028 to 2031 at a 12.5bp facility fee, and drew nothing on it — a filing three weeks old that no wire covered.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No financing event appears in the baseline's eight reactions; this line has never moved the name on the record available, which is why it is sized near zero.
findings.why_not_priced: It is not priced because nobody wrote about it, and it is worth almost nothing, which is the honest answer rather than a reason to size it up. I asked the question the money answers and got the benign one: undrawn at signing, a 12.5bp facility fee and a three-year maturity extension are what a syndicate underwrites for a company with no leverage problem, and the stated use is 'working capital and other general corporate purposes, including capital expenditures and acquisitions'. It corroborates the M&A capacity management named as a priority after spending $300m on Elgen and LSI in FY2026 on $170m of free cash flow. It is filed so that the financing line on this name reads as 'checked, benign' and cannot later be mistaken for distress.
findings.independence: Corroborated by a different document: the 14 August Canaccord presentation 8-K sets out $170m FY2026 free cash flow at 102% conversion and $300m of acquisition spend — https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000108516/000119312526350842/wor-ex99_1.htm (2026-08-14).

outside_window.finding: The Investor and Analyst Day — the company's first since October 2023 — is 10 November 2026, a month and a half after this print. It is the event the 15 September 8-K actually announced and the one the ~10% re-rating is anticipating, so the substance behind the run-up is scheduled outside anything this trade can experience.

searched_and_found_nothing: Form 4 activity around the 16 September pop — the only filings on 2026-09-21 are Hayek's 5.55 and Chan's 4.40 phantom shares from deferred-comp dividend reinvestment at $57.38, with aff10b5One false; no insider sold into the re-rating (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/108516/000119312526396484/ownership.xml)

Today's 2026-09-22 press release is a flat $0.20 quarterly dividend plus the retirement of three directors (Endres, Horton, Winland, 97 years combined) — no dividend action and no buyback news to trade, and it is already public before the close (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/09/22/3366739/0/en/worthington-enterprises-declares-quarterly-dividend-recognizes-contributions-of-three-retiring-directors.html)
An acquisition announced with the print — the revolver and the CEO's 'strategic M&A' language make one possible but nothing is sourceable, so it is not a finding

Retail sell-through for the propane/torch/celebrations business — Home Depot +1.7% comps, Lowe's +0.2%, Tractor Supply -1.5% with weakness in 'seasonal big-ticket', all consistent with the resilient-consumable picture management already described and none of it specific enough to Bernzomatic/Coleman/Balloon Time to size
A company-level ClarkDietrich or non-residential framing datapoint for June-August 2026; ClarkDietrich is private and discloses nothing, so the trough claim is unverifiable from outside
Hiring pages, status pages, app-store data and support forums — not meaningful surfaces for a steel-converting industrial
A second confirmation that the 2025-09-23 print was a consensus beat; the +48% adjusted EPS move is from the release itself and I did not claim a beat I could not source
baseline_tension: It agrees with the baseline rather than beating it on direction — the +3.93 put skew, the +8.74% five-day run-up and the free control all point the same way I do — so the only part that is genuinely mine is WHY the run-up exists (a name-only 8-K that disclaims financial effect, sitting on a $13m-a-quarter business already disclosed in June) and the correction to the baseline's own reaction history, which reads 3-of-8 up at a 3.56% median because it pools four non-earnings item-2.02 filings; on the four real releases it is 0-of-4 up at a mean of -6.2%.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until the company or a direct counterparty has said it, and a public series is partly priced): cut the steel-cost finding from -2.0 to -1.5, and rewrote why_not_priced to concede the 5.1% 90-day estimate cut is analysts already marking HRC down, while adding Armstrong's 'price actions intended to offset rising steel costs' as the counterparty attestation that keeps it a finding rather than a macro guess.

Lesson 3 (your own caveat has to reach the number; resolve a self-defeating finding rather than sizing it): cut the WAVE/Armstrong finding from +1.5 to +0.8, because my own text says the August price actions land at the end of Worthington's quarter and so are mostly a Q2 FY2027 event — the draft had sized the H2 step-up as if it were in this quarter.

Lesson 9 (size a segment finding net of the rest of the company): added the explicit net line to the steel finding — Consumer/Trade & Specialty is ~38% of sales, grew 4% with 10% EBITDA growth, is consumable rather than big-ticket, and HD/Lowe's comps for the overlapping period were positive — which is part of why the size came down rather than up.

Lesson 8 (thin coverage means a confirmed fact moves more, and understatement is the systematic error) combined with Lesson 1 (the reaction function has veto power, in both directions): moved expected_move_pct from -4.0 to -4.5 even though the finding sum got smaller (-3.2 to -3.4), because the veto here runs the other way from usual — the name's own real-earnings reaction distribution (0 of 4 up, mean -6.2%) is worse than my evidence, on a five-analyst name.

Lesson 1 and the 'asking what the market missed generates pessimism' note: moved print_vs_bar_pct from -2.5 to -1.0. I could not source a documented reason to expect an EPS miss beyond a steel cost analysts have already cut for, against $13m of guided incremental data-centre revenue, LSI at 40% EBITDA margins annualising and a bar cut 5.1%. The honest fundamental read is roughly in line; the widened gap between -1.0 and -4.5 IS the answer to the second question.

Lesson 3's contradiction rule, applied in the draft and kept: the data-centre ramp was NOT filed as a separate positive finding alongside the rename-deflation negative — they rest on the same disclosure and one sign had to win, so the ramp lives inside finding 1's band and its independence note says so.

Lesson 6 (verify the bar): confirmed $0.75 / $331.3m from two agreeing sources before sizing, so no small-size cap applies; and moved the 10 November Investor Day to outside_window rather than letting the event the run-up is actually about sit in the key.

Lesson 7 (positioning is the thing to beat): left standing — short interest at 3.5% of float and 5.18 days to cover gives no squeeze mechanism to shrink the negative for, but the skew agreement is the stated reason -4.5 is well inside the -6.2 base rate.
